newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Heated Belgian Renault workers clash with police.
newsitem.headline: Heated Belgian Renault workers clash with police.

text.p: Belgian police on Friday turned water cannon on irate Renault SA workers who were marching in their hundreds through central Brussels in protest at plans to shut down their Belgian car plant.
Protesters clashed with police as they threw eggs and stones and tried to break through a barricade in front of the offices of the Flemish regional government in Brussels.
There were no reports of injuries or arrests.

Up to 900 people joined the protest - with about half the crowd made up of disillusioned workers from bankrupt Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq throwing fire crackers and shouting "Renault must stay open" as they marched.
A small delegation was received in the cabinet of Flemish regional president Luc Van de Brande.

The demonstrators continued past the French embassy and were then due to march on to the offices of Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, who is on a visit to Latin America, and of European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
